jcr:content.jcr:description: An open coastal headland above Sand Bay, with rocky ground and far-reaching views.
jcr:content.shortDescription: An open coastal headland above Sand Bay, with rocky ground and far-reaching views.

placeabout.heading: About this place
placeabout.description:
Sand Point projects into the Bristol Channel north of Weston-super-Mare. Its grassland and limestone landscape make a rewarding walk for families who enjoy a more exposed countryside outing.

Use the National Trust route guide to plan your walk and allow longer than an adult walking pace. Our family idea: stop well away from the edges and look for birds using the wind above the headland.

placepracticalinfo.heading: Practical information
placepracticalinfo.bestFor: Older children and families used to uneven countryside paths.
placepracticalinfo.facilities: A car park serves the walk; refreshments can be found in nearby Kewstoke.
placepracticalinfo.parking: Use the Sand Point car park and check the current parking tariff.
placepracticalinfo.goodToKnow: The circular route has steep sections, uneven ground and stiles. Supervise children near drops and keep dogs controlled around livestock.

placevisitmap.travelNote: Use the Sand Point car park and check the current parking tariff. Use this postcode for the arrival area, then follow local signs to the entrance. Google Maps can use your current location, or you can enter a starting point.
